name: Marcus Bell

five_sec.what_is_it: An AI meal-planning app that picks dinners and nudges you with notifications.
five_sec.who_for: Families who want the decision taken away entirely.
five_sec.trust_why: 90,000+ families is a real-sounding number, but the primary call to action is a CEO letter, not a product action. That's a strange workflow.
five_sec.next_step: Find the pricing page and check whether Kroger is supported.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The mockup is a menu app with 'Replace' and 'Modify' buttons on a recipe card.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Pricing is metered by 'messages': $25/month for 150. For a meal planner. And the grocery handoff is Instacart, Walmart or Amazon Fresh, no Kroger.
full_page.whats_missing: Kroger, a servings setting, and anything about schedules beyond a date picker.

OL.quote: Top-ups at $0.30 a message. I'm not budgeting text messages to find out what's for dinner on a baseball night.

five_sec.what_is_it: A weekly dinner planner where the family votes by text and the list goes to Instacart or Walmart.
five_sec.who_for: Households where more than one person has opinions about dinner. Mine.
five_sec.trust_why: Plain statement that they don't deliver food and 'no card needed' up front. No App Store rating shown, and it's a company I've never heard of.
five_sec.next_step: Jump to pricing and find where Kroger fits.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It says so in bold under the paragraph: 'We don't deliver food. We plan your week and send your grocery list.'

full_page.what_stopped_me: Kroger cart is on the paid Family plan, and nothing explains whether that's a real cart push or a deep link. The iPhone app is iPhone only; I'm on a Pixel, so it's 'Add to Home Screen'.
full_page.whats_missing: How it handles practice nights (it mentions 'cook nights' and time to cook, not a calendar), and a sample for 5 people instead of 4.

DD.quote: Kids reply with numbers, top five become the week, Kroger cart on Family at $39 a year. That's an actual workflow, not more recipes.

five_sec.what_is_it: Recipe organizer with a meal calendar and grocery list.
five_sec.who_for: People who already collect recipes and like to plan.
five_sec.trust_why: 4.8 App Store, 4.7 Google Play, both shown. That's the kind of proof I check anyway.
five_sec.next_step: Look at how the grocery list gets to a store.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: 'Recipes, Meal Plans and Grocery Lists, All in One App'.

full_page.what_stopped_me: It's a toolbox. I still pick every recipe. And the store handoff is a vague 'grocery delivery' line, no Kroger named.
full_page.whats_missing: Suggested meals; a clear Kroger integration.

PTE.quote: Pricing page is the most honest of the bunch: $49 a year, no surprise renewals. But 'an app for do-ers' means I'm still doing it.

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal-kit delivery, with a 'pick a mystery box' offer pop-up.
five_sec.trust_why: A gamified offer pop-up is exactly the sales gimmick I avoid.
five_sec.next_step: Dismiss and look for a price. There isn't one.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Meal boxes on screen; I've had them.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Prices behind a zip code; fine print says shipping on every box after the first. For five people with a teenager it was never sustainable.

HF.quote: '10 Free Meals' is 'based on total discount given on first box for a 4-person, 5-recipe plan.' I've read enough fine print for one evening.

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal plan subscription with a video hero.
five_sec.trust_why: Established brand, but the first screen is a video and a generic slogan.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The how-it-works graphic is a phone with a checklist; step 2 sends a list to grocers.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Price is buried in a collapsed FAQ; trial renews into paid. Kroger is listed though, and there's a 30 Minute plan.
full_page.whats_missing: Price on the page, servings, and how practice nights would work.

EM.quote: Kroger logo, 30 Minute plan, two million customers. Then 'How much does eMeals cost?' is a closed accordion. Classic.

dd_offer.why: The pricing block and FAQ spell it out: Family free 14 days, no card, add a card from Account to keep it, otherwise you drop to Free.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: Family features switch off and I'm on the free plan unless I've added a card. Nothing gets charged.

head_to_head.reason: It's the only one built around the household deciding together, and the Kroger cart is $39 a year.

EM.reason: Both reach Kroger, but DinnerDrop shows its price and lets the family vote instead of me texting everyone.

PTE.reason: Plan to Eat organizes recipes I don't have; DinnerDrop picks the dinners.

OL.reason: $3.25 a month with Kroger beats $25 a month in metered messages without it.

HF.reason: Kits for five cost too much and took 40 minutes; DinnerDrop sends groceries I already buy.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Pricing page (/start): explain how the Kroger cart push actually works with a screenshot, and show a 5-person, practice-night example week, plus say plainly how Android users install it.
